'''Bismack Biyombo Sumba''' (born August 28, 1992) is a Congolese professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected seventh overall in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]] and subsequently traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]].

Biyombo played four seasons for the Bobcats (rebranded to the Hornets in 2014) before signing with the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the 2015 off-season, with whom he reached the [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]] in 2016. He then signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] in the 2016 off-season and played two seasons with the team before being traded back to the Hornets in the 2018 off-season.

After three seasons during his second stint in Charlotte, Biyombo signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in January 2022 and spent two seasons with the team. He then played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] during the 2023–24 season before joining the Spurs in February 2025. With San Antonio, he reached the [[2026 NBA Finals]].

==Early life and career==
Biyombo was born in [[Lubumbashi]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Zaire]] (now the [[Democratic Republic of Congo]]), to parents François and Françoise Biyombo. He has three brothers named Billy, Biska and Bikim, and three sisters named Bimeline, Bikelene and Bimela.<ref name=":1" />

At age 16, he played for Lupopo in the [[2008 FIBA Africa Clubs Champions Cup]], Africa's premier senior league at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bismack Biyombo - Player Profile |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/168283/Bismack-Biyombo |access-date=August 8, 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball }}</ref> That year he was discovered by coach [[Mário Palma]] at a youth tournament in [[Yemen]]. His play impressed Palma and earned him an opportunity to train in Spain.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwc/men/v1/news/lateNews/p/newsid/45604/FE_news_lateNews_arti.html|title=COD/ESP – Palma not surprised by the new sensation of the ACB, Bismack Biyombo|last=Chitunda|first=Julio|date=January 21, 2011|website=FIBA.COM|access-date=May 12, 2016|archive-date=June 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610143822/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwc/men/v1/news/lateNews/p/newsid/45604/FE_news_lateNews_arti.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Biyombo started the 2009–10 season with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada B|Fuenlabrada-Getafe]] in the Spanish fourth-tier [[Liga EBA]] before moving to [[CB Illescas]] in the Spanish third-tier [[LEB Plata]]. He started the 2010–11 season with CB Illescas before moving to [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] of the first-tier [[Liga ACB]] in January 2011.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/players/bismack/biyombo/202687|title=Bismack Biyombo stats, details, videos, and news|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Fuenlabrada (2011)===
Biyombo made his debut at age 18 in the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]] against [[DKV Joventut]] on January 9, 2011, recording 5 points and 7 rebounds in just over 13 minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/fichas/LACB55131.php|title=DKV Joventut – Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|date=January 9, 2011|website=ACB|access-date=May 12, 2016|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170837/http://www.acb.com/fichas/LACB55131.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> In Fuenlabrada's narrow defeat to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], he recorded 6 points and 3 blocks,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/fichas/LACB55148.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110119004731/http://www.acb.com/fichas/LACB55148.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2011|title=Real Madrid – Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|date=January 16, 2011|website=ACB|access-date=May 12, 2016}}</ref> one of them against former [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|Spanish League MVP]] and [[Spanish national basketball team|Spanish national team]] player, [[Felipe Reyes]].<ref name=":0" />

At the [[Nike Hoop Summit|2011 Nike Hoops Summit]], Biyombo participated for the World Select Team (against the USA Select Team), and recorded a triple double, with 12 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 blocks. It was the first recorded triple-double in the Summit's history.<ref name=":1" />

===Charlotte Bobcats / Hornets (2011–2015)===
[[File:Bismack Biyombo 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Biyombo with the Charlotte Hornets in 2014]]
Biyombo was drafted seventh overall by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]], but his rights were later traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in a draft night trade.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/110623_release_draft.html|title=Bobcats Select Walker, Acquire Biyombo and Maggette|date=June 23, 2011|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 12, 2016}}</ref> On December 19, 2011, Biyombo signed a multi-year deal with the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_biyombo_111219.html|title=Bobcats Sign Bismack Biyombo|date=December 19, 2011|work=NBA.com|access-date=May 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126074650/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_biyombo_111219.html|archive-date=January 26, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> After averaging five points per game over his first two seasons with Charlotte, Biyombo's minutes and subsequent production dropped dramatically in 2013–14 as he fell out of favor with coach [[Steve Clifford]], as he averaged just 2.9 points in 13.9 minutes per game.

The Bobcats changed their name to the ''Hornets'' ahead of the [[2014-15 NBA season|2014-15 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hornets all the buzz in Charlotte |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10958580/charlotte-bobcats-officially-change-nickname-hornets |website=ESPN |date=May 20, 2014 |access-date=May 20, 2014}}</ref> While his forte in defense and rebounding did drop in 2013–14, Biyombo began the 2014–15 season in much better form despite missing seven out of the first eight games of the season largely due to the acquisition of [[Jason Maxiell]] in the 2014 off-season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wasserman |first=Jonathan |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2259380-bismack-biyombos-nba-career-looking-like-its-already-on-life-support |title=Bismack Biyombo's NBA Career Looking Like It's Already on Life Support |work=BleacherReport.com |date=November 7, 2014 |access-date=December 13, 2014}}</ref> With the late-December injury to center [[Al Jefferson]], Biyombo was placed into the starting line-up.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasybasketball/update/24923855/bismack-biyombo-to-replace-injured-al-jefferson-in-hornets-lineup|title=Bismack Biyombo to replace injured Al Jefferson in Hornets' lineup|last=Hurcomb|first=Michael|date=December 30, 2014|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=May 12, 2016}}</ref> On June 30, 2015, the Hornets decided not to extend a qualifying offer to Biyombo, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13170834/charlotte-hornets-extend-qualifying-offer-bismack-biyombo|title=Hornets don't extend qualifying offer to Bismack Biyombo|date=June 29, 2015|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 11, 2016}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2015–2016)===
On July 18, 2015, Biyombo signed a two-year, $5.7 million contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/biyombo-071815|title=Raptors Sign Bismack Biyombo|date=July 18, 2015|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 12, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/bismack-biyombo-thanks-raptors-fans-time-toronto/|title=Bismack Biyombo thanks Raptors, fans for time in Toronto|date=July 6, 2015|website=sportsnet.ca|access-date=October 28, 2016}}</ref> On August 1, 2015, he played for Team Africa at the [[NBA Africa Game 2015|2015 NBA Africa exhibition game]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13359599/nba-current-former-stars-put-show-africa-exhibition|title=NBA stars, legends shine in Africa exhibition|date=August 1, 2015|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 12, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Raptors in the team's season opener against the Indiana Pacers on October 28, recording 7 points and 5 rebounds in a 106–99 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|title=DeRozan scores 25, Lowry has 23, Raptors beat Pacers 106–99|last=Harrison|first=Ian|date=October 28, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=May 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160520142811/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Biyombo started in 18 straight games between mid-November and late December while [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] was recovering from a fractured hand. On December 17, he recorded 8 points, a then career-high 18 rebounds, and a career-high tying 7 blocks in a loss to the Charlotte Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151217/TORCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Lin scores 35 points, Hornets beat Raptors 109-99 in OT|last=Kiser|first=Bill|date=December 17, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160406104449/http://www.nba.com/games/20151217/TORCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 6, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Five days later, he recorded 9 points and a then career-high 20 rebounds in a 103–99 win over the Dallas Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151222/DALTOR/gameinfo.html|title=DeRozan helps Raptors edge Mavericks 103-99|last=Girard|first=Daniel|date=December 22, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151223000946/http://www.nba.com/games/20151222/DALTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 23, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Biyombo returned to a bench role on December 30.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151230/WASTOR/gameinfo.html|title=DeRozan scores 34 as Raptors edge Wizards 94-91|work=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2015|access-date=December 31, 2015}}</ref> He returned to the starting line-up in mid-March with Valančiūnas out injured again. On March 17, 2016, Biyombo scored a career-high 16 points and set a franchise record with 25 rebounds in guiding the Raptors to a 101–94 overtime win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160317/TORIND/gameinfo.html|title=Lowry, DeRozan each score 28 in 101-94 win over Pacers|last=Skirvin|first=Jeff|date=March 17, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160320093225/http://www.nba.com/games/20160317/TORIND/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 30, he recorded seven points and six rebounds in a 105–97 win over the Atlanta Hawks, helping the Raptors record a 50-win season for the first time in franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160330/ATLTOR/gameinfo.html|title=Raptors beat Hawks 105-97 to notch first 50-win season|last=Girard|first=Daniel|date=March 30, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 31, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402061641/http://www.nba.com/games/20160330/ATLTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 2, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The Raptors finished the regular season as the second seed in the Eastern Conference with a 56–26 record. In the first round of the playoffs, the Raptors faced the seventh-seeded Indiana Pacers, and in a Game 5 win on April 26, Biyombo recorded 10 points and 16 rebounds off the bench to help the Raptors take a 3–2 series lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160426/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|title=DeRozan scores 34, Raptors rally for 3-2 lead over Pacers|last=Harrison|first=Ian|date=April 26, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160713231955/http://www.nba.com/games/20160426/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=July 13, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Raptors went on to win the series 4–3, moving on to the second round where they faced the Miami Heat. In Game 7 of the Raptors' series with the Heat, Biyombo recorded 17 points and 16 rebounds as a starter in a 116–89 win, helping the Raptors advance to the conference finals for the first time in franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160515/MIATOR/gameinfo.html|title=Lowry scores 35, DeRozan has 28, Raptors beat Heat 116-89|work=NBA.com|date=May 15, 2016|access-date=May 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171004061057/http://www.nba.com/games/20160515/MIATOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> In Game 3 of the conference finals against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Biyombo set a Toronto playoff record with 26 rebounds, helping the Raptors cut the Cavaliers' advantage in the series to 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160521/CLETOR/gameinfo.html|title=DeRozan, Raptors end Cavaliers' streak with 99-84 win|work=NBA.com|date=May 21, 2016|access-date=May 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521034519/http://www.nba.com/games/20160521/CLETOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 21, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Raptors went on to lose the series in six games.

After declining his $2.9 million player option for the 2016–17 season, Biyombo became an unrestricted free agent on June 7, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/report-raptors-biyombo-opts-contract-becomes-ufa/|title=Report: Raptors' Biyombo opts out of contract, becomes UFA|work=sportsnet.com|date=June 7, 2016|access-date=October 28, 2016}}</ref> Biyombo later revealed that he wished to re-sign with the Raptors, but with the re-signing of [[DeMar DeRozan]], the Raptors did not have the salary cap space to make it possible.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://raptorsrapture.com/2016/07/10/loss-bismack-biyombo/|title=Loss of Bismack Biyombo hurts Raptors|work=raptorsrapture.com|date=July 10, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://clutchpoints.com/bismack-biyombo-opts-contract-still-interested-toronto/|title=Bismack Biyombo opts out of his contract, could still be interested in Toronto|work=clutchpoints.com|date=July 10, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2016–2018)===
[[File:Bismack Biyombo, Markieff Morris (33122074442).jpg|thumb|Biyombo (right) with the Orlando Magic in 2017, defended by [[Markieff Morris]]]]
On July 7, 2016, Biyombo signed a four-year, $72 million contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-bismack-biyombo|title=Magic Sign Bismack Biyombo|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2016/7/2/11946100/bismack-biyombo-four-year-deal-orlando-magic-nba-free-agency-2016|title=Bismack Biyombo signs a 4-year, $72 million deal with the Orlando Magic, per report|work=sbnation.com|date=July 2, 2016|access-date=October 28, 2016}}</ref> After exceeding the flagrant foul limit during the 2016 playoffs, Biyombo was forced to serve an NBA-mandated one-game suspension to begin the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899378|title=Whiteside powers Heat to season-opening win|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Magic in the team's second game of the season on October 28, scoring two points in just under 23 minutes in a 108–82 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899454|title=Pistons roll in home opener, 108-82 over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=October 28, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> On January 16, 2017, he scored a season-high 15 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He tied that mark on February 11, scoring 15 points against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On March 5, he grabbed a season-high 15 rebounds against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/biyombi01/gamelog/2017/|title=Bismack Biyombo 2016-17 Game Log|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 1, 2018}}</ref>

On January 1, 2018, Biyombo recorded 13 points and a season-high 17 rebounds in a 98–95 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975291|title=Allen, Crabbe help Nets beat Magic 98-95|work=ESPN.com|date=January 1, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2018}}</ref> On January 12, he scored a career-high 21 points in a 125–119 loss to the Washington Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975366|title=Beal, Wall score 30 apiece; Wizards down Magic 125-119|work=ESPN.com|date=January 12, 2018|access-date=January 12, 2018}}</ref> On April 4, he had 12 points, 12 rebounds and a career-high five assists in a 105–100 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975916|title=Jamel Artris has career-high 18, Magic hold off Mavs 105-100|work=ESPN.com|date=April 4, 2018|access-date=April 4, 2018}}</ref>

===Return to Charlotte (2018–2021)===
On July 7, 2018, Biyombo was traded back to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in a three-team deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-biyombo-and-two-second-round-draft-picks|title=Hornets Acquire Biyombo and Two Second-Round Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2018|access-date=July 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Denton|first=John|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-jerian-grant-and-timofey-mozgov-three-team-trade-20180708|title=Magic Acquire Jerian Grant and Timofey Mozgov in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2018|access-date=July 8, 2018|quote=the Orlando Magic acquired point guard Jerian Grant and reserve center Timofey Mozgov on Saturday night.}}</ref> On January 5, 2019, he scored a season-high 16 points in a 123–110 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071252|title=Jokic scores season-high 39, Nuggets beat Hornets 123-110|work=ESPN.com|date=January 5, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2019}}</ref>

On November 27, 2019, Biyombo recorded a season-high 19 points along with 9 rebounds and two blocks in a 102–101 win against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Season Recap: Hornets Lean Heavily on Bismack Biyombo For Leadership, Experience|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/season-recap-hornets-lean-heavily-bismack-biyombo-leadership-experience|url-status=live|access-date=November 20, 2021|website=Charlotte Hornets|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200702001044/https://www.nba.com/hornets/season-recap-hornets-lean-heavily-bismack-biyombo-leadership-experience |archive-date=July 2, 2020 }}</ref> On December 16, 2019, he logged a season-high 17 rebounds along with 11 points and a block against the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bismack Biyombo pulls down a season-high 17 rebounds in loss|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/243018/bismack-biyombo-pulls-down-season-high-17-rebounds-loss.php|url-status=live|access-date=November 20, 2021|website=FantasyPros|date=December 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211120195626/https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/243018/bismack-biyombo-pulls-down-season-high-17-rebounds-loss.php |archive-date=November 20, 2021 }}</ref>

|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211120180613/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hornets-bismack-biyombo-scores-13-points-in-loss/ |archive-date=November 20, 2021 }}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2022–2023)===
Biyombo became an unrestricted free agent after the [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=3 Remaining NBA Free Agents Who Could Help a Contender|url=https://medium.com/sportsraid/3-remaining-nba-free-agents-who-could-help-a-contender-407664de990a|url-status=live|access-date=November 20, 2021|website=Medium|date=September 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927112634/https://medium.com/sportsraid/3-remaining-nba-free-agents-who-could-help-a-contender-407664de990a |archive-date=September 27, 2021 }}</ref> He did not sign with any team throughout 2021 in part due to him grieving for the passing of his father, François.<ref>[https://andscape.com/features/my-dad-was-everything-to-me-bismack-biyombo-is-still-healing-in-his-nba-return/ ‘My dad was everything to me’: Bismack Biyombo is still healing in his NBA return]</ref> On January 1, 2022, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]] via the COVID-19 hardship exemption.<ref>{{cite web |title=Phoenix Suns to sign C Bismack Biyombo, per report |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2952030/phoenix-suns-to-sign-c-bismack-biyombo-per-report/ |website=Arizona Sports |access-date=January 1, 2022 |date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> On January 11, Biyombo signed for the rest of the season after showing off some very positive production during his 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suns officially sign veteran Bismack Biyombo for rest of season|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2022/01/11/suns-officially-sign-veteran-big-bismack-biyombo-rest-season/9172840002/|access-date=January 23, 2022|website=AZ Central}}</ref> On January 17, Biyombo had 17 points and 14 rebounds. Five days later, on January 22, Biyombo recorded 21 points, 13 rebounds, and 5 assists coming off the bench. From January 26–30, Biyombo became a starter once again due to injuries to [[Deandre Ayton]] and [[JaVale McGee]]. In the 17 games Biyombo played from January to February 12, the Suns were undefeated.

On July 5, 2022, the Suns re-signed Biyombo.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Suns Re-sign Bismack Biyombo |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-re-sign-bismack-biyombo |access-date=July 11, 2022 |website=Phoenix Suns |language=en}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2023–2024)===
On November 1, 2023, Biyombo signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Bismack Biyombo|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-bismack-biyombo|website=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2023|access-date=November 2, 2023}}</ref> but was waived on January 10, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Vince Williams Jr. to multi-year contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-vince-williams-jr-to-multi-year-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2024|access-date=January 10, 2024}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2024)===
On February 10, 2024, Biyombo signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Bismack Biyombo|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/signs-biyombo-240210|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> On March 6, Biyombo unexpectedly collapsed to the floor on his team's sideline during a game against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He was eventually able to leave the court under his own power and was cleared of any serious medical condition.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Quinn |first1=Sam |title=Thunder center Bismack Biyombo collapses on sideline, but serious medical issue ruled out, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/thunder-center-bismack-biyombo-collapses-on-sideline-but-serious-medical-issue-ruled-out-per-report/ |website=CBS Sports |date=March 7, 2024 |access-date=March 7, 2024}}</ref>

=== San Antonio Spurs (2025–2026) ===
On February 9, 2025, Biyombo signed a 10-day contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Stinar | first=Ben | title=San Antonio Spurs Reportedly Sign 13-Year NBA Player | website=Yardbarker | date=2025-02-08 | url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/san_antonio_spurs_reportedly_sign_13_year_nba_player/s1_16925_41721424 | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref> On February 21, Biyombo and the Spurs agreed to another 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Spurs Sign Bismack Biyombo to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-bismack-biyombo-to-second-10-day-contract|access-date=February 27, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> On March 3, the Spurs signed him to a contract for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs sign center Bismack Biyombo for remainder of season|url=https://foxsanantonio.com/sports/san-antonio-spurs-sign-center-bismack-biyombo-for-remainder-of-season-texas-bexar-county-points-rebounds-blocks-players-nba-basketball-frost-bank-center|access-date=March 30, 2025|website=foxsanantonio.com|language=en}}</ref> In 28 appearances (26 starts) for San Antonio, Biyombo averaged 5.1 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.1 assists.

On September 15, 2025, Biyombo re-signed with the Spurs on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Spurs, center Bismack Biyombo agree to a 1-year deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46270529/sources-spurs-center-bismack-biyombo-agree-1-year-deal|access-date=December 21, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Biyombo is [[Catholic Church|Catholic]].<ref name=":2" /> He enjoys reading in his spare time and speaks five languages: English, French, [[Lingala]], Spanish and [[Swahili language|Swahili]].<ref>{{cite web |title=PLAYER BIO |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/player/202687/bismack-biyombo/bio |access-date=14 December 2022}}</ref> Biyombo is eligible to play for the [[DR Congo men's national basketball team]], but never played for the team, despite his intentions to do so in November 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=It's official: Biyombo to suit up for DR Congo in 3rd window of African Qualifiers |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/african-qualifiers/news/it-s-official-biyombo-to-suit-up-for-dr-congo-in-3rd-window-of-african-qualifiers |access-date=August 8, 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

After fainting during an NBA game in 2024 due to [[dehydration]], Biyombo revealed that he has been [[Fasting in religion|fasting]] regularly for 13 seasons as a personal devotion to his Catholic faith.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=NBA player faints during game, reveals he fasts regularly as a part of Catholic Faith | date=April 19, 2024 |url=https://catholicvote.org/nba-player-faints-during-game-reveals-he-fasts-regularly-as-a-part-of-catholic-faith/?mkt_tok=NDI3LUxFUS0wNjYAAAGSmeBvXy0oQzCM1nQpDcsmNES8ElMmYelAkf4Qcv94-n8JMfnqIW7FBB61lJ22CUrw7NXJlmL1SsVAYeYajYN5njqehaiCg4OLYEp8y3zx}}</ref>

Biyombo started the Bismack Biyombo Foundation in 2016. During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] in 2020, the foundation donated around $1 million worth of medical supplies to people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=The Congolese NBA Veteran Whose Heart, and Generosity, Never Left Home|url=https://time.com/6103209/bismack-biyombo-next-generation-leaders/|url-status=live|access-date=November 20, 2021|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211013230434/https://time.com/6103209/bismack-biyombo-next-generation-leaders/ |archive-date=October 13, 2021 }}</ref> In March 2022, Biyombo announced that he had pledged his salary from the entire 2021–22 season towards the construction of a hospital in Congo, in honor of his father.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Suns C Bismack Biyombo pledges entire 2021-22 salary to build hospital in honor of late father |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/suns-c-bismack-biyombo-pledges-entire-2021-22-salary-to-build-hospital-in-honor-of-late-father/ar-AAUXuOP |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=MSN |language=en-US}}</ref>
